answer: Agents can admit a new identity only after it completes a useful task that established peers verify, with each peer staking tokens on the result. A trellis of overlapping reviewers makes it hard for one operator to approve all its own aliases; caught collusion burns the reviewers’ stakes and revokes the identities. To flood the network, an attacker must fund many distinct tasks and risk real collateral for each alias, so a dawn of fresh accounts cannot cheaply overwhelm the system or hide in a canyon of names.
